title.narrative: FAO resilience rapid respons Burkina Faso 2018-2022
FAO resilience rapid respons Burkina Faso 2018-2022

description.narrative:
Project name: "Réponse d’urgence et appui à l’amélioration de la résilience des populations vulnérables dans les zones à risque du Burkina Faso 2018-2021" ("Urgent response aiming at strengthening the resilience of vulnerabe households in risk zones in Burkina Faso 2018-2020"). The FAO project code is OSRO/BKF/801/SWE.
Agreement partner and implementor: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), United Nations
In Burkina Faso, poor rainfall distributions in recent years have reduced the area of cereal crops and the income generated by agriculture The joint SAP-GTP mission in October 2017 counted 83 municipalities at risk. Thus, the current crop year 2017-2018 cereal production was estimated to have decreased with 12% compared to the average for the last five years.
The project reaches 28,000 poor and very poor households (according to the HEA classification) in the coverage regions, all of whom will benefit from the unconditional cash transfer during the lean season. In addition to unconditional cash transfer, 4100 self-selected households will have the opportunity to enroll in the «Cash for Work" activities (i.e. rehabilitation of communal infrastructures) during the mitigation and recovery period. Moreover, according to their main livelihoods, all households (HH) will receive productive assets: 2800 HH cereal production, 2500 HH small livestock restocking (sheep, goats, poultry, pigs depending on the choice), 1900 HH with livestock feed coupons and 2500 HH for market gardening coupled with nutritious gardens to strengthen their resilience. All targeted households (10 000) will also benefit from a nutritional education/sensitization programme.
Among the targeted beneficiaries, special emphasis will be placed on women and young people in order to take into account their specific needs.
Development objective: The resilience of vulnerable pastoralists and agro-pastoralists to climate and economic shocks is improved. The initial agreement had an activity period from 1 June 2018 to 31 May 2020 and a budget of 79 million SEK. The agreement was amended at end 2019 with a budget increase up to 129 million SEK. A second amendment was made at end 2020 with an extension of the activity period to 31 December 2021 and a budget increase up to the total of 189 million SEK. The amendments are justified by the dramatic increase of need for support to the local population due the worsened security situation and the increase of the number of internally displaced people to more than one million.

Projektnamn: "Réponse d'urgence et appui à l'amélioration de la résilience des populations vulnérables dans les zones à risque du Burkina Faso 2018-2021" ("Akut svar för att stärka moståndskraften hos utsatta hushåll i riskzoner i Burkina Faso 2018-2021"). FAO:s projektkod är OSRO/BKF/801/SWE.
Avtalspartner och genomförare: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), FN
I Burkina Faso har den i tid och rum ojämnt spridda nederbörden under de senaste åren minskat den odlade arealen och den inkomst som genereras av jordbruket. Det gemensamma SAP-GTP-uppdraget i oktober 2017 klassade 83 kommuner i riskzonen för matosäkerhet och visade att skörden 2017-2018 minskade med 12% jämfört med genomsnittet för de senaste fem åren.
Det aktuella FAO-projektet bistår ca 28000 fattiga och mycket fattiga hushåll (enligt HEA-klassificeringen) i det täckta området, vilka alla kommer att dra nytta av överföringen av "unconditional cash" under de svåra månaderna före skörd. Förutom "unconditional cash" kommer 4100 hushåll ha möjlighet att anmäla sig till aktiviteterna "Cash for Work" (dvs. rehabilitering av kommunala infrastrukturer) under höst och torrperiod. Dessutom kommer hushållens egna produktiva kapacitet att stärkas genom utdelning av "produktions-kits": 2800 kits för spannmålsproduktion, 2500 kits för uppfödning av boskap (får, getter, fjäderfä, grisar beroende på valet), 1900 hushåll får djurfoderkuponger och 2500 hushåll får stöd i grönsaksodling för att stärka nutrition och motståndskraft. Alla hushåll i målgruppen kommer också att dra nytta av utbildning i nutrition.
Utvecklingsmål: De sårbara pastoralisternas och agro-pastoralisternas motståndskraft mot klimat och ekonomiska chocker förbättras. Det initiala avtalet mellan ambassaden och FAO sträckte sig fram till 31 maj 2020 för en budget om 79 miljoner kr. Hösten 2019 ökades budgeten till 129 miljoner kr. Hösten 2020 ökades den ytterligare till 189 miljoner kr och aktivitetsperioden förlängdes till 31 december 2021. Skälet till budgetökningen var det dramatiskt ökade behovet av stöd till befolkningen i norra landet pga den tilltagande säkerhetskrisen och den stora ökningen av internflyktingar (drygt en miljon under hösten 2020).

This contribution aims to increase the resilience against climate chocks and economic chocks for vulnerable pastoralist and agro-pastoral households.
Activities are conducted under three result areas:
Results 1: Vulnerable households improved their access to food and means of production
- Unconditional monetary assistance during the lean season - Carry out post-distribution monitoring studies - Support and strengthen food security alert and analysis system
Result 2: The agro-sylvo-pastoral production capital of vulnerable households in the provinces heavily affected by the crisis is restored
- Support households for animal fodder production - Distribution of fodder production seed and organic fertilizer - Support households for food production - Distribution of chickpea seed and fertilizer for food crops for the benefit of women - Support households for vegetable production - Distribution of vegetable seeds and fertilizer for organic gardening - Support for the creation of sustainable water mobilization infrastructure - Realization of boulis and establishment of infrastructure management committee - Support for the consolidation of peace - Creating conflict sensitive platforms - Set up awareness/training platform on issues for prevention and management of community conflicts
Result 3: The nutritional situation of vulnerable households in the provinces heavily affected by the crisis in Burkina Faso is improved
- Training in production and broadcasting of radio programs - Production of communication materials - Conditional cash transfer for nutritional purposes for the benefit of pregnant and breastfeeding women and families with children aged 0 to 5 years
________________________________
The 2022 extension period will also further focus on consolidating previous results made in the three result areas, by using a triple-Nexus approach "Humanitarian-Development-Peace", in the following focus areas:
1) Strengthening gender equality and target people with specific needs:
- Strengthen the promotion of gender equality by addressing the specific needs of each group and by targeting at least 50% women and 50% young people, taking into account the degrees of vulnerability;
- Take into account people with specific needs, disabilities, minorities or marginalized groups.
2) Strengthening the value chain approach and nutrition:
- Strengthen the value-chain approach from production to marketing, including the processing of food, animal and non-timber forest products; - Address the issues of malnutrition through the prevention and management of malnutrition in children under five years, by strengthening training and raising awareness among the population; - Develop a cash and nutrition package for families with children under 5 years.
3) Strengthening structuring and sustainable production investments:
- Contribute to the strengthening of the productive capacities of households with the creation of infrastructures for improved water management (boulis, pastoral drilling, etc.), recovery of degraded land and support for vocational training of beneficiaries; - Diversify food production by supporting the development of rice and vegetable gardening; - Develop income-generating activities, particularly for women and young people, in connection with the promotion of local and artisanal products.
4) Strengthening peace building through social cohesion and conflict prevention:
- Set up mechanisms for the prevention and management of conflicts, in particular through Dimitra clubs and village savings and credit associations; - Organize consultations on land- and peace issues between local actors; - Organize debates and awareness sessions on land law, land management and the peaceful management of land conflicts through local radio stations with the involvement of trained young people; - Compilation of texts relating to land and distribution to local structures and actors.

Despite deteriorated security situation in the three target regions, the project recorded a satisfactory rate of achievement of aimed targets. Overall, the average rate of achievement of project targets is 74%. Also, compared to the baseline situation, most of the indicators aimed at assessing the performance of the project have seen a marked increase.
The impacts of the project on women and girls includes testimonies of satisfaction from the beneficiaries were reported. These include testimonies on sheep distribution, cowpea production and the cash support. FAO considers that it will be necessary to wait for the results of post distribution monitoring studies to provide tangible evidence.
The support in improved rice seeds and mineral fertilizer was a great help for the beneficiaries who harvested about 2,800 tons. This production will largely cover the rice needs of host households and IDPs and also generate a surplus for sale, in order to improve their income.
Result 1: Vulnerable households have improved their access to food and means of production.
A total of 19,868 households benefited from cash support (out of 20,872 planned; 95.18%). The cash support represents 37% of the budget in 2021.
77% of beneficiary households did not resort to negative coping strategies. Only 18% used stress strategies, 0.6% crisis strategies and 4.4% emergency strategies. The proportion of households with negative coping strategies decreased significantly between the baseline year and the midpoint, dropping from 58% to 23%.
58% of beneficiary households have daily access to two meals during the lean season (on average). Households with access to three meals a day represent 39%. The situation differs from region to region, in the Centre-Nord region this proportion is the highest at 45%, compared to 31% in Sahel. The diet of the majority of beneficiary households (68%) is moderately diversified with access to 3 to 6 food groups. Households with low dietary diversity represent 30%. The Sahel has the highest proportion as 47% of households have a low Dietary Diversity Score (SDA) with less than 3 food groups, compared to 16% in the Centre-Nord.
The gender analysis shows a higher proportion of female-headed households (36.3%) with an acceptable food consumption score, compared to 31.5% of male-headed households.
Cash support in all its forms (unconditional emergency cash, unconditional lean cash and cash for work) has strengthened the purchasing power and dignity of beneficiaries by enabling them to obtain basic necessities for their choices.
The cash support has made it possible to develop a form of solidarity between individuals and to strengthen social cohesion within the community. The majority of beneficiaries (85%) who received the cash transfer shared it with non-beneficiaries in the same village. The food purchased with cash support was used to feed beneficiary households, but also to feed relatives who did not benefit from the support. Other uses of the cash support are for health, children's schooling and clothing needs.
In terms of protecting livelihoods, cash transfer assistance has enabled vulnerable households to reduce the use of erosive coping strategies. The money received during the lean season was used to pay for food and build up a stock to get through this difficult period. The stock enabled the beneficiary owners of fields to meet the physical conditions for a better success of the agricultural production campaign. Beneficiaries of cash for work, in addition to the cash consideration received after the completion of the work (personal or collective), were usefully occupied during the dry period when some were forced to leave in search of income. Cash for work also enabled the majority of beneficiaries to restore their fields in order to improve their productivity.
Result 2: The agro-sylvo-pastoral production capital of vulnerable households in the provinces strongly affected by the crisis is reconstituted
- 450 ha developed for an estimated production of 330 tonnes of fodder to meet the feed needs of 3,800 small animals and 800 large animals. - 187.5 tons of animal feed provided, accompanied by training to all beneficiary households. - 11,250 animals were vaccinated and de-wormed for more than 3650 beneficiaries. - 1050 sheep were given to 350 beneficiary households. - Development of three sites of 1 ha per region, corresponding to 9 ha for the benefit of 500 beneficiaries. - Production of 7000 tons of tomatoes and 4000 tons of onions. - 2800 tons of rice produced for an average yield of 4 tons/ha (compared to 2 tons/ha in sites without support). - 60,000 cuttings (about 180,000 plants as 3 nodes/cuttings) were made available to 3000 beneficiaries. - Support for 750 women for cowpea production.
The average area exploited by beneficiary households is 2.9 ha. Households in the Center-North have the largest cultivated areas, i.e. 3.22 ha, compared to 3.06 ha and 2.53 ha, respectively in the North and in the Sahel. Only 28% of the available land is farmed by women, the rest by men. The average areas compared to the reference situation show a decrease of 9% overall. Only the Center-North region experienced an average increase in surface area of 15%. The North and Sahel regions experienced declines in average surface areas, of 10% and 26% respectively. These decreases would be largely linked to the security situation in these two regions.
The average cereal production per household is estimated at 1.647 kg, up 80% compared to the 2018 crop year. The increase was higher in male-headed households (89%) and lower in households led by women (70%). At the regional level, the variations are 129% in the North, 58% in the Centre-North and -24% in the Sahel.
Production increases in both regions would be linked to input support and improved seeds, combined with good rainfall conditions. As for the drop in production in the Sahel, it could be explained by the absence of beneficiaries of cereal production, but also by the abandonment of crops due to insecurity.
The average production per household of other speculations is estimated at 666 KG in 2020, against 458.5 KG in 2018, an increase of 45%. Regional disparities are significant. Indeed, the North region recorded a significant increase of 131%, while the Centre-North recorded a quasi-stability (1%) and the Sahel a drop of around 40%.
Result 3: The nutritional situation of vulnerable households in the provinces strongly affected by the crisis is improved
Several of the activities of this result area are planned to be implemented during 2022, during the one year extension phase of the contribution. Preparations have been done during 2021 to plan for the implementation of activities.
Cereals are the most frequently consumed food group as 98.5% of women consumed cereals the day before the survey. Dark green leaves (vegetables) are the second most consumed group of 62.5%.
Women of reproductive age have a dietary diversity score of 2.82 (standard deviation of 1.41). At the regional level, the score is higher in the Centre-Nord (3.57 overall). The Sahel region has the lowest overall score of 2.46. Women of childbearing age with an acceptable SDA (greater than or equal to 5) represent 13.8%. At the regional level, this proportion is 24.5% in the Center-North, 12.4% in the Sahel and 8.4% in Nord.
57% of children 0-23 months were breastfeed. Centre-Nord has the highest rate of 97% of children that breastfeed, followed by the Sahel region (51%) and the North region (46%). Overall, the proportion of children who continue to be breastfed up to one (1) year is 97.6%. Compared to the baseline, there is an improvement in the proportion of children aged 12 to 15 months still breastfed in the Centre-Nord, which has gone from 96.2% in 2018 to 100% in 2021. These values have increases in all three regions of the project between 2018 to 2021.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
